title: Ink Wash
look: Chinese ink wash: grey ink pooling at the edges, a dry-brush contour, empty paper and a red seal.

doc.essence: A brush painting in one stick of ink diluted to many greys: soft wet areas that darken where the water dried, a quick contour, most of the sheet left empty, and the painter's red seal.
doc.notIt: Not ink (no colour, wet grey washes and a seal), not pencil (brush and wash, not graphite hatching), not ukiyo-e (no colour, no carved key line, no composed stage).
doc.shapes: A dark contour that sits a little transparent, and a pale grey copy of the silhouette offset beside it, the way ink bleeds into damp paper.
doc.colour: Every colour becomes a grey of the same lightness. Areas are lighter in the middle and pool darker at their edges. Only the seal is red.
doc.motion: Smooth, with a slight boil on the brush line.
pitfalls: Characters whose colours share a lightness turn into one grey: the contour separates them.
Keep the stage sparse: the empty paper is part of the look.
